newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end higher on late blue-chip buying.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end higher on late blue-chip buying.

text.p: * Speculative thirdliners focus of investor interest
Late-session accumulation of select blue-chips propelled the Philippine stock index out of the tight range it had been locked in for most of the day, brokers said.
The 30-share index rose 24.41 points, or 0.73 percent, to close at 3,363.08 points after staying within a narrow 10 point band through most of the session.
Earlier, thirdliners and penny stocks were in focus, brokers said.

"People are still in love with (thirdliner) oil and mining stocks," Allan Araullo, vice president of Regina Capital Development Corp, said. Many tertiary issues, most of them dormant companies, are rising on speculation they will be converted into holding firms.
"Many of them are not just rumours, but there are solid assets which are being put into these companies," Jose Ricardo Garcia, vice president of Diversified Securities, added.
Interest shifted back to blue chips Ayala Land Inc and San Miguel Corp B before the market closed by noon, as some investors cashed in on the steep rise of penny issues.
Gainers outnumbered losers two to one, amidst moderate turnover of slightly more than 3.0 billion pesos.
